Connectors

Eight crates implement Source and Sink. Each one has its own page, naming the crate to depend on, the constructor to call, and the keys its config node accepts.

In one line
One crate per transport, added only when you move bytes that way
You need
The connector crate for a Rust pipeline; on pcs-service, its connector-* feature, plus a transformer-* feature wherever the connector carries a byte format
Read this if
You are choosing a transport. The page for the one you picked has its constructor signature, its config keys and the errors it raises

The nine at a glance

ConnectorConfig typeDirectionformatRun modeFeature
Channel ChannelSource, ChannelSink source and sink none any connector-channel
File FileSource, FileSink source and sink required any connector-file
PostgreSQL PostgresSource, PostgresSink source and sink none any connector-postgresql
Kafka KafkaSource, KafkaSink source and sink optional, ndjson stream, unless stop_at_end = true or compacted = true connector-kafka
NATS NatsSource, NatsSink source and sink optional, ndjson stream, unless stop_at_end = true connector-nats
TCP tcp source and sink optional, arrow-ipc stream for the source, any for the sink connector-tcp
DataFusion SQL none source none Rust only none
S3 S3Source, S3Sink source and sink required any connector-s3
HTTP HttpSource, HttpSink source and sink required any connector-http

Two ways in

A connector is reached either by calling its constructor in Rust and handing the result to Pipeline::add_source, or by naming its type string in the service config and letting the factory build it. The second path needs the connector's feature on pcs-service, because register_builtin_factories only installs what is compiled in.

TOMLthe dependency form is the same for all eight
# In a clone of the repository.
pcs-connector-file = { path = "crates/pcs-connector-file" }

# Outside one. The crates are not published to crates.io.
pcs-connector-file = { git = "https://github.com/nassor/pcs" }

Every connector depends on pcs-core with its io feature, so the Source and Sink traits arrive with it. Nothing here depends on pcs-service: the factory contract lives in pcs-connector, below the host, so a connector compiles without wasmtime, axum or redb in the graph. Each page above states the constructor, every config key and the errors that key can raise.

Writing your own

An out-of-tree connector is a crate that depends on pcs-core for the traits and pcs-connector for SourceFactory and SinkFactory, and on nothing else of PCS. Both traits build through fn build(&self, config: &ConfigValue, ctx: &ConnectorContext<'_>), where ctx resolves the format key against the transformer registry so no connector owns a list of formats. A custom binary then chains register_source or register_sink onto register_builtin_factories. Registering a type_name that is already taken replaces the earlier factory.
